title: Strata schemes and management rights schemes
subject: This guide explains how the managed investment provisions of the Corporations Act 2001 apply to arrangements involving real property under strata or community title, and outlines conditional relief from certain provisions for operators and promoters of strata schemes and management rights schemes.
background: The guide is issued under the Corporations Act 2001 and the ASIC Act. It is intended for operators and promoters of properties managed for investors, such as serviced apartments, hotels, motels, and resort complexes. It provides guidance on when such arrangements constitute managed investment schemes and the relief available from licensing, disclosure, and hawking obligations.
ruling: ASIC considers that many strata and management rights schemes may be managed investment schemes under the Corporations Act. ASIC has provided conditional relief via ASIC Corporations (Serviced Apartment and Like Schemes) Instrument 2016/869, exempting eligible operators from the managed investment, AFS licensing, product disclosure, and hawking provisions, subject to conditions such as disclosure to investors and compliance with certain requirements. The guide sets out ASIC's interpretation of key concepts like 'common enterprise' and 'interests' in the context of real property arrangements. ASIC also outlines its approach to granting individual relief where the class order does not apply.
legislation_referenced: Australian Securities and Investments Commission Act 2001 (Cth) s 12DA
